flags.note: "considérants" and "dispositif" — these are legal terms from French procedure. "Considérants" are the recitative or preamble clauses of a judgment (the "whereas" or "considering that" clauses stating reasons); the "dispositif" is the operative or dispositive clause — the actual decision or order. Tocqueville's irony is that the minority claims to argue reasons without issuing commands, but the distance between the two is unstable. "Whereas clauses" and "therefore" capture this in plain English; "preamble" and "operative clause" are more technical alternatives. READING flag follows.
